solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Painter a little like author Roald, some might say?

indicators.note: the question mark and this phrase tell us the clue words are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: somewhat like the children's writer Roald Dahl, which could be called Dahl-y

explanation.surface: A question about whether a painter resembles the writer of Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Something a bit like Dahl could be called Dahl-y, which is said the same way as the surname of the Spanish surrealist.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dalí was a Spanish surrealist artist famous for melting clocks.

clue.text: European acrobat jumping about in University Challenge?

indicators.note: an acrobat leaping around suggests these letters being thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A European gymnast bouncing around on a TV quiz show.
explanation.walkthrough: University Challenge looks like the British TV quiz, but here it describes the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing race on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boat Race is a rowing contest between two universities, so it is literally a challenge between universities.

clue.text: Society girl upset titled gent? Rubbish!

parts.note: a deb, or debutante, is a young woman making her entry into high society

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: A debutante has upset an aristocrat, who dismisses it as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered waste or remains, a synonym of rubbish as a noun.

clue.text: Located in Budapest, a terraced property

indicators.note: the answer is located inside the run of letters in these words

parts.note: the six letters run across the end of Budapest, the word a and the start of terraced

explanation.surface: An estate agent's line about a terraced house found in Budapest.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the end of Budapest, the word a and the start of terraced.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a piece of landed property, or a person's total assets.

clue.text: In time, traitor will make mistakes

indicators.note: one word placed in another: the traitor's word goes in the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is slang for someone who betrays their associates

explanation.surface: A prediction that a traitor will eventually slip up.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are errors in a printed book, listed with their corrections; the word is Latin plural for errors.

clue.text: Briefly woo typist who won't be there long?

definitions.text: typist who won't be there long?

indicators.note: a word cut short, here losing its final letter

parts.note: to woo is to try to win over or entice, to tempt

explanation.surface: A man making a quick pass at a passing office typist.
explanation.definitionFit: A temp is a temporary office worker, traditionally a secretary hired for a short spell.

clue.text: Word in America for end of bus line?

parts.note: a term is a word or expression
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking what Americans call the final stop on a bus route.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as asking for an American word, but America simply supplies the two-letter country abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is the final station or stop on a transport route.

clue.text: Boat sure to be blown up — by me?

definitions.text: Boat sure to be blown up — by me?

indicators.note: an explosion scatters the letters, signalling they are rearranged

parts.note: these two words supply exactly the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wrecker gloats that a vessel is certain to be destroyed by them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the anagram, and the boast of someone who sabotages a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately destroys or damages property, such as blowing up a ship.

clue.text: Observation about suitable victim

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
a mark is a target for a con artist

explanation.surface: A comment about someone who would make an easy target.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a comment, something said as an observation.

clue.text: An old queen falls in Africa

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the British monarch who reigned 1837 to 1901
second meaning: the great waterfall on the Zambezi between Zambia and Zimbabwe

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch takes a tumble while in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Falls looks like a verb, as if the queen trips, but it is the noun for a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: The waterfall was named by Livingstone after the reigning British monarch of that name.

clue.text: Descendant of Homer is found in LA

indicators.note: one word sits found inside another

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A genealogical claim that a descendant of the Greek poet lives in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: Homer suggests the ancient poet, but it is Homer Simpson of the cartoon, whose daughter has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Simpsons, Lisa is Homer's clever elder daughter, so his direct offspring.

clue.text: I prepared mint tea for close friend

indicators.note: making a drink means working the ingredients into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone brewed a herbal infusion for a dear companion.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, an intimate is a very close friend or confidant.

clue.text: Smacking His Majesty on bridge

indicators.note: in an across clue, the king's word comes on, or after, the bridge's word

parts.note: a span is the part of a bridge between supports, or a bridge itself
the title used for a king

explanation.surface: Someone slapping the monarch while standing on a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanking means hitting someone on the bottom with the open hand, a form of smacking.

clue.text: Swine, the boxer, having change of heart

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: pug is short for pugilist, a boxer

explanation.surface: Calling a fighter a swine, then he changes his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxer suggests the dog breed, and a pug is also a dog, but here pug is slang for a prizefighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A swine is a pig, both the farm animal and a term of abuse for an unpleasant person.

clue.text: Angora OK to make a jumper?

indicators.note: the letters are used as raw material to make something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: these words supply exactly the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether angora wool is acceptable for knitting a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is British for a sweater, which fits the angora wool, but here it means an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: The kangaroo is the Australian marsupial famous for moving by hopping.

clue.text: Guide regularly argues for cheapest class

parts.note: to steer is to guide or direct

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one of the word

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of argues

explanation.surface: A tour guide routinely argues the case for economy travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the lowest-priced passenger accommodation on a ship, near the rudder.

clue.text: Declares English to be hostile

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly or assert

explanation.surface: Someone announces that the English will be unfriendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse means opposed or disinclined, close in sense to hostile towards something.

clue.text: Catch Parisian in revolutionary district

parts.note: en is the French word for in

indicators.note: something revolving turns round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a part is a region or area, as in parts of the country

explanation.surface: Arresting a Frenchman in a district that is hotbed of revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: Parisian looks like a person, but together with in it means the French translation of in.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to catch, as in a snare or by trickery.

clue.text: Oddly neglected house in New York making you curious

indicators.note: the odd-position letters of the word are ignored, leaving the even ones

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of house, once the odd ones are dropped

explanation.surface: A rundown New York house arouses your curiosity.
explanation.walkthrough: Neglected house reads as a run-down building; it means the second and fourth letters of house sit inside NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosy means prying or inquisitive, an unpleasant kind of curious.

clue.text: Reportedly draw a woman from Bangkok?

indicators.note: as it is reported, that is spoken, so a word sounding the same is wanted

parts.note: a tie is a match ending level

explanation.surface: Supposedly an artist sketches a woman from Thailand's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Draw suggests sketching, but it is a drawn game; the question mark marks a woman as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangkok is the capital of Thailand, so a woman from there is a Thai.

clue.text: Charm one's way in?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to delight or captivate, a verb stressed on the second syllable
second meaning: a door or gateway, a noun stressed on the first syllable

explanation.surface: How a smooth talker gets past the door.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are spelt the same but pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance is to hold spellbound, while an entrance is the opening by which someone goes inside.

clue.text: Sailors about to visit Cracow on vacation

indicators.note: the word for about goes into the other, as a visitor goes inside
vacated, emptied of its inside, leaving only the first and last letters

parts.note: Cracow emptied of its inner letters leaves just its first and last
re means concerning

explanation.surface: A ship's company plans a holiday trip to the Polish city.
explanation.walkthrough: Cracow is an older English spelling of Kraków, in Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is the group of people who work a ship.

clue.text: Priest who's not been celibate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the title for a Catholic priest
second meaning: a man who has had a child, so has not abstained

explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies a scandal about a priest; the second sense just means a man who has begotten a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic priests are addressed as Father, and any man who has sired a child is a father.

clue.text: Maybe winter edition will be made more spicy?

parts.note: winter is one example of a season, hence maybe

explanation.surface: A cookbook's winter edition will have hotter recipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoned food has had salt, pepper or spices added to improve its flavour.

clue.text: Fancy shoving teacher into river?

indicators.note: one word is pushed inside another
the teacher's word goes into the river's word

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
pupils in Britain address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: Pupils wondering whether to push their teacher into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a British river, one of several of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Desire as a noun is a longing or wish, the same as a fancy for something.
